rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the opening takbir, Allahu akbar means that God is greater and more exalted than everything.
rows.anchor: ومعناه الله أعظم وأجل من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True takbir leaves no other greatness, remembrance, love, or desire in the heart alongside God; otherwise the speaker's state contradicts the words.
rows.anchor: فينبغي أن لا يكون في تلك الحالة في قلبك عظمة شيء آخر وأمارة ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual intoxication is heedlessness, which prevents nearness to God just as literal drunkenness prevents understanding prayer.
rows.anchor: كما لا تجدون القربة وأنتم سكارى من الغفلات أيضا لا تجدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness is conditioned on prostration, as the command to prostrate and draw near states.
rows.anchor: لأن القربة مشروطة بشرط السجود كما خوطب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration means descending from the mount of one's existent attributes, carried by divine generosity to the threshold of divine being and a vision of beauty and majesty; this is the secret of sitting for tashahhud after prostration.
rows.anchor: والسجود أن تنزل من مركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual major impurity is attachment to the lowly world, which makes the seeker deserving of distance from God.
rows.anchor: لا تجدونها مع جنابة استحقاق البعد وهي ملابسة الدنيا الدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may cross worldly concerns only by the outward path of sacred law, taking food and drink to preserve life, clothing for protection and modesty, and sex to preserve offspring.
rows.anchor: إلا على طريق العبور بقدم ظاهر الشرع في سبيل الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual washing is achieved through nearness, repentance, sincere seeking, good intention, and purity of purpose from worldly attachment and desire.
rows.anchor: بماء القربة والإنابة وصدق الطلب وحسن الإرادة وخلوص النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual illness is a heart whose disposition has become crooked in seeking the Real.
rows.anchor: بانحراف مزاج القلب في طلب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual travel is wavering among pursuit of this world, the afterlife, and the Lord.
rows.anchor: التردد بين طلب الدنيا وطلب العقبى والمولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming from the privy signifies following one's caprice.
rows.anchor: من غائط تتبع الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Touching women signifies engagement in worldly occupations, which estranges the seeker from God after nearness to the sacred precincts and gardens of intimacy.
rows.anchor: أي لابستم الأشغال الدنيوية فأجنبتم وتباعدتم عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lacking water signifies inability to repent and return sincerely to God by turning away from created beings.
rows.anchor: بالإعراض والانقطاع عن الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pure earth is the dust of the feet of virtuous spiritual masters, cleansed of bad character and deeds.
rows.anchor: وهو تراب أقدام الرجال الطيبين من سوء الأخلاق والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiping the face and hands means taking the masters' dust and clinging to their generous hems, submitting sincerely to their guidance.
rows.anchor: أذيال كرمهم مستسلمين بصدق الإرادة لأحكامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may pardon sectarian attachment and failure to turn wholly to Him, and may pardon worldly contamination through this praiseworthy spiritual discipline.
rows.anchor: يعفو عنكم التعصب وعدم الانقطاع إليه بالكلية ولعله يعفو عنكم التلوث بالدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives traces of misery left by desire's dust; those who keep company with the virtuous attain felicity, for their companions do not suffer.
rows.anchor: غبار الشهوة فإنهم يسعد بهم لأنهم قوم لا يشقى بهم جليسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed Persian poem urges one to weep and apologize for one's failings while life and speech remain, and to value this precious opportunity.
rows.anchor: كنونت كه شمست اشكى ببار زبان در دهانست عذري بيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī distinguishes three levels of associating partners with God, each answered by a corresponding level of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن للشرك مراتب وللمغفرة مراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Overt shirk, typical of ordinary people, is worshipping idols, planets, or other entities; it is forgiven through tawhid, affirming servanthood inwardly and outwardly while recognizing God's lordship.
rows.anchor: فالشرك الجلي بالأعيان وهو للعوام وذلك بأن يعبد شيء من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidden shirk, typical of the elect, mixes worship with attention to the world, ego, or anything besides God; its cure is exclusive devotion of the one to the One.
rows.anchor: والشرك الخفي بالأوصاف وهو للخواص وذلك شوب العبودية بالالتفات إلى غير الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most hidden shirk, for the especially elect, is perceiving otherness and selfhood; its cure is unity, the annihilation of human nature in the enduring divine identity.
rows.anchor: والشرك الأخفى وهو للأخص وذلك رؤية الأغيار والأنانية فلا يغفر إلا بالوحدة

words: وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who seeks forgiveness from these levels of shirk may be forgiven at the corresponding level; associating partners erects a great barrier between the person and God.
rows.anchor: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء أي لمن يشاء المغفرة فيستغفر الله تعالى من مراتب الشرك

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asserting the existence of things and one's own ego creates the greatest veil; a Persian verse calls one's own existence a sin beyond comparison.
rows.anchor: فقد افترى إثما عظيما أي جعل بينه وبين الله حجابا من إثبات وجود الأشياء وأنانيته

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the Prophet expresses amazement at Jews who claim purity from sin and say they are God's children and beloved, despite their disbelief and grave sins.
rows.anchor: خطاب للنبي عليه السلام على وجه التعجيب

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording also warns anyone who boasts of exceptional piety, obedience, or closeness to God against admiring their own deeds.
rows.anchor: واللفظ عام يشتمل كل من زكى نفسه ووصفها بزيادة التقوى والطاعة والزلفى عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God truly purifies those among His believing servants who merit it, since He knows the good and evil concealed within a person.
rows.anchor: تزكيته ممن يستأهلها من المرتضين من عباده المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fatil is the tiny thread in a date stone's cleft, a proverbial measure for the least possible injustice; injustice would add to punishment or subtract from reward.
rows.anchor: وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة يضرب به المثل في القلة والحقارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not wronged by the punishment they receive for their ugly deed.
rows.anchor: أي يعاقبون بتلك الفعلة القبيحة ولا يظلمون في ذلك العقاب

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks in what state they fabricate lies about being God's children and purified; explicitly calling fabrication a lie intensifies condemnation, though fabrication already entails falsehood.
rows.anchor: والتصريح بالكذب مع أن الافتراء لا يكون إلا كذبا للمبالغة في تقبيح حالهم

words: انظر كيف يفترون على الله الكذب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabrication alone suffices to condemn them, apart from its connection to self-purification and their other grave sins.
rows.anchor: من حيث هو افتراء عليه تعالى مع قطع النظر عن مقارنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs here mean the Qur'an and the other miracles.
rows.anchor: القرآن وسائر المعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawfa can signal a threat or warning, as here, and can also signal a promise, adding emphasis.
rows.anchor: كلمة تذكر للتهديد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means admitting the unbelievers into a vast, dreadful fire.
rows.anchor: ندخلهم نارا عظيمة هائلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skins' ripening means their being burned through.
rows.anchor: {كلما نضجت جلودهم} أي احترقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here other skins differ in form, not underlying identity: the very same skin is remade in another form, as metal is melted and shaped into a different ring.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أنه يعاد ذلك الجلد بعينه على صورة أخرى كقولك صغت من خاتمي خاتما غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent objection is that replacing a burned, sinful skin with an unoffending one would punish the innocent; the answer is that the sensitive skin that sinned is punished, and its identity remains one.
rows.anchor: قلت : العذاب للجلدة الحساسة وهي التي عصت لا للجلد مطلقا والذات واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasting means their experience of punishment continues without interruption or diminution, like wishing someone lasting increase in honor.
rows.anchor: أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع كقولك للعزيز أعزك الله أي أدامك على عزك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Fire consumes them seventy times each day; each time they are told to return, they return as they were.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : تأكلهم النار في كل يوم سبعين مرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet describes an unbeliever's skin as forty cubits, his tooth as large as Uhud, and his upper lip reaching his navel, with running worms, camel-neck snakes, and mule-sized scorpions between flesh and skin.
rows.anchor: وروي مرفوعا أن جلد الكافر أربعون ذراعا وضرسه مثل أحد وشفته العليا تضرب سرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such added size and creatures do not punish an innocent new body; the added weight itself burdens the sinner, like Hell's chains, fetters, snakes, and scorpions.
rows.anchor: لكن إذا زيد ذلك ثقلة على العبد ويكون نفس الثقل عقوبة عليه كسائر عقوبات جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although they already suffer severely, tasting describes how each renewed exposure is felt like tasting something, without pain fading through burning or continued exposure.
rows.anchor: إحساسهم بالعذاب في كل مرة كإحساس الذائق بالمذوق من حيث أنه لا يدخله نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Renewing the skins makes clear that sensation persists, since people might otherwise imagine that burning destroys perception; God could preserve perception or bodies without this renewal.
rows.anchor: ولعل السر في تبديل الجلود مع قدرته تعالى على بقاء إدراك العذاب وذوقه بحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty, so nothing can prevent what He wills for wrongdoers, and wise in the punishment He assigns.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع عليه شيء مما يريده بالمجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker in intense longing may swear by God's beauty and majesty for a fragment of divine approach and union, but such an oath is idle under the law of contentment and a lapse under the path of surrender; God pardons it from weakness.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن الطالب الصادق عند غلبات الشوق ووجدان الذوق يقسم عليه بجماله وجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker should instead yield to God's decrees of acceptance or rejection and approach or estrangement, preferring steady service over honor, closeness, vision, or union; this reading is cited from al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya.
rows.anchor: أن الأولى الذوبان والجمود بحسن الرضى بحسب جريان أحكام المولى في القبول والرد والإقبال والصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed Persian poem says not to waste time: opportunity is precious and time is a sword.
rows.anchor: مكن وقت ضايع فافسوس وحيف كه فرصت عزيز ست والوقت سيف

rows.speaker: ابن الفارض
rows.claim: Ibn al-Farid urges decisive use of time and warns that postponing things with 'later' is a dangerous affliction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الفارض قدس سره

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi verses continue the exhortation to patience amid worldly hardship and in seeking the beloved Lord.
rows.anchor: أي كه صبرت نيست از دنياي دون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the fourth of four verses revealed about wine; Bursevī says its fuller discussion occurred in al-Baqara, and wine includes every intoxicant.
rows.anchor: هذه هي الآية الرابعة من الآيات الأربع التي نزلت في الخمر وقد سبق التفصيل في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir means every kind of gambling, including backgammon, chess, fourteen-piece games, dice, and gambling with an egg.
rows.anchor: القمار كله فيدخل فيه النرد والشطرنج والأربعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anṣāb are idols set upright for worship; the singular is naṣb, with an open nūn and still ṣād.
rows.anchor: أي الأصنام المنصوبة للعبادة واحدها نصب بفتح النون وسكون الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azlām are divining arrows marked with commands, prohibitions, or left blank; pre-Islamic Arabs drew them at the Kaaba before travel, war, or trade, repeating a blank draw to learn their allotted fortune.
rows.anchor: هي سهام مكتوب على بعضها أمرني ربي وعلى بعضها نهاني ربي يطلبون بها علم ما قسم من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs is filth that sound reason finds repugnant.
rows.anchor: قذر يعاف عند العقول أي تكرهه وتنفر منه العقول السليمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najās is usually what nature finds filthy, while rijs is more often what reason finds filthy; these sins are called rijs because they must be avoided like repulsive filth.
rows.anchor: والرجس بمعنى النجس إلا أن النجس يقال في المستقذر طبعا والرجس أكثر ما يقال في المستقذر عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This phrase describes rijs as arising from Satan's work of embellishing it, urging it, and making it attractive to its perpetrators.
rows.anchor: صفة لرجس أي رجس كائن من عمله أي من تزيينه لأنه هو الداعي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to keep away from this impurity; its apparent force is obligation, with success hoped for through avoidance.
rows.anchor: أمر بالاجتناب وهو تركه جانبا وظاهر الأمر على الوجوب

words: إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَن يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ ٱلْعَدَٰوَةَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine causes worldly enmity because drunk drinkers brawl; an Anṣārī once struck Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas with a camel's jawbone.
rows.anchor: أما العداوة في الخمر فهي أن الشاربين إذا سكروا عربدوا وتشاجروا كما فعل الأنصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gambling causes enmity when a man wagers family and property, loses them, and is left grieving and angry with his fellow gamblers.
rows.anchor: وأما العداوة في الميسر فهي أن الرجل كان يقامر على الأهل والمال ثم يبقى حزينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every enemy is hateful, but not everyone who hates is an enemy.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين العداوة والبغضاء أن كل عدو مبغض بلا عكس كلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'in wine' attaches causally to 'cause', as in the hadith about a woman entering Hell because of a cat.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى في الخمر متعلق بيوقع على أن تكون كلمة في هنا لإفادة معنى السببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine and gambling receive special emphasis because believers are being addressed and their prohibition is the main purpose; adding idols and divining arrows heightens censure by grouping four similarly harmful practices.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الخمر والميسر تنبيها على أنهما المقصودان بالبيان لأن هذه الآية خطاب مع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional time clause is governed by its answer, 'turn away'; the address is to the Prophet and his community.
rows.anchor: إذا منصوب بجوابه وهو فأعرض والمراد بالخطاب النبي عليه السلام وأمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawḍ literally means beginning to engage in something, but conventionally refers to engaging in falsehood; the signs here are the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والخوض في اللغة الشروع في الشيء مطلقا إلا أنه غلب في الشروع في الشيء الباطل والآيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh disbelieve, mock, or attack the Qur'an, leave their gatherings and get up from them.
rows.anchor: بالتكذيب والاستهزاء به والطعن فيه كما هو دأب كفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continue to leave until they discuss something other than God's signs; the pronoun is grammatically masculine because the signs are treated as discourse or Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي استمر على الإعراض إلى أن يشرعوا في حديث غير آياتنا فالضمير إلى الآيات والتذكير باعتبار كونها حديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-imma derives from in plus the added ma, with the conditional nūn assimilated into it.
rows.anchor: أصله إن ما فأدغمت نون إن الشرطية في ما المزيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Satan might make the Prophet forget is the instruction to stop sitting with them.
rows.anchor: ما أمرت به من ترك مجالستهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the reminder means after remembering; dhikra is a verbal noun, and the source says no other verbal noun follows this fu'la pattern.
rows.anchor: بعد أن تذكره فهو مصدر بمعنى الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who put denial and mockery where belief and reverence belong.
rows.anchor: الذين وضعوا التكذيب والاستهزاء موضع التصديق والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording makes forgetting a mere possibility, not an event that must have occurred; scholars agree that prophets may experience forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإنساء محض احتمال يدل عليه كلمة إن الشرطية فلا يلزم وقوعه مع أن العلماء قد اتفقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan here may mean Iblis or one of his chief troops, since the Prophet's companion had become Muslim and only urged good, unlike the companion of ordinary people.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان إبليس أو واحد من أكابر جنوده لأن الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet was favored over Adam because his Satan became Muslim with God's help and his wives supported him, whereas Adam's Satan and wife supported his sin.
rows.anchor: كان شيطاني كافرا فأعانني الله عليه فأسلم وكان أزواجي عونا لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims objected that leaving whenever the Qur'an was mocked would prevent them from sitting in the Sacred Mosque and circumambulating the Kaaba; God therefore allowed them to remain to admonish and remind.
rows.anchor: لئن كنا نقوم كلما استهزؤوا بالقرآن لم نستطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falq means splitting something apart; al-habb denotes grain seeds such as wheat, barley, and corn, which God splits to bring out a green shoot.
rows.anchor: الحب : جمع حبة وهي اسم لجميع البزور المقصودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nawā is the hard pit inside fruits such as peaches, apricots, and dates; God splits it to bring out a leafy, branch-bearing tree.
rows.anchor: واحدتها نواة وهي الشيء الموجود في داخل الثمر مثل نواة الخوج والمشمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, God brings growing life in animals and plants from non-growing things such as sperm and seeds.
rows.anchor: بيان لما قبله أي يخرج ما ينمو من الحيوان والنبات مما لا ينمو من النطفة والحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversely, God brings non-growing sperm and seeds from living animals and plants; 'living' and 'dead' are metaphors for growing and inert, though life literally entails sensation and voluntary motion.
rows.anchor: فالحي والميت مجاز عن النامي والجامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some instead take the words literally: God brings a living human from dead sperm and a dead egg from a living chicken.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حمل اللفظ على الحقيقة وقال يخرج من النطفة الميتة بشرا حيا ومن الدجاجة بيضة ميتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brings a believer from an unbeliever, an unbeliever from a believer, a disobedient person from an obedient one, a scholar from an ignorant person, and an intelligent person from a fool, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يخرج المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The palm of faith grows from the dead seeds of the letters in the declaration of divine oneness, while the deadness of hypocrisy emerges from that same living declaration.
rows.anchor: يخرج نخل الإيمان من نوى الحروف الميتة في كلمة لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the One of great power and stature, God alone, who deserves worship.
rows.anchor: {الله} المستحق للعبادة وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks how people can be turned away from worshipping God to another; ifk means to invert or turn something aside, and the address is to Quraysh because the sura is Meccan.
rows.anchor: والإفك في اللغة قلب الشيء وصرفه والخطاب لكفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faliq al-isbah is another predicate of inna; isbah, with a kasra on its first letter, is a verbal noun for entering daylight and names the dawn.
rows.anchor: خبر آخر لإن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits the dawn's column from the whiteness and spreading light of day.
rows.anchor: أي فالق عمود الفجر عن بياض النهار وإسفاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is repose because those tired by daytime rest in it, or because creatures dwell in it; the source links this to the wording of Yunus 10:67.
rows.anchor: يسكن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته من سكن إليه إذا اطمأن إليه استئناسا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the sun and moon follow different cycles that measure time: the sun completes a year and the moon a month, regulating seasons, crops, cultivation, and reproduction.
rows.anchor: على أدوار مختلفة يحسب بها الأوقات فإنه تعالى قدر حركة الشمس بمقدار من السرعة والبطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a ḍamma, hisābān means calculation and counting; with a kasra, hisbān means conjecture and guesswork.
rows.anchor: فالحسبان بالضم مصدر بمعنى الحساب والعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing lunar phases and new moons let people know debt deadlines and other appointed times, so the sun and moon are instruments for reckoning.
rows.anchor: وباختلاف منازل القمر وتجدد الأهلة في كل شهر يعلم آجال الديون ومواقيت الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun precedes the moon because of its brightness and its primacy as the source of celestial light; the stars' light is borrowed from it according to their orientation and clarity.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الشمس لضيائها على القمر لأنها معدن الأنوار الفلكية من البدور والنجوم

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
rows.claim: Aftadeh Efendi says the moon's light comes from the realm of lights rather than its own essence; its apparent deficiency results from gradual density, enabling people to know months and years.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي قدس سره

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
rows.claim: He describes the sun and moon as the very entities of this manifestation, their outward faces directed upward, while their visible inner sides alternately open and close like eyes.
rows.anchor: والشمس والقمر عينا هذا التعين وظاهرهما إلى الفوق والذي نراه جانبهما الداخل

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
rows.claim: He says stars are not embedded in the moon but appear through reflected light in its subtle veins; a shooting star is like the sun moving from place to place, knowledge known to spiritual wayfarers rather than philosophers.
rows.anchor: والكواكب ليست مركوزة فيه وإنما هي بانعكاس الأنوار في بعض عروقه اللطيفة

rows.speaker: حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي
rows.claim: In the afterlife, night and day are not darkness and light but are known by other signs of divine manifestation; one leaf of the referenced tree brought to earth would illuminate the world.
rows.anchor: الليل والنهار في عالم الآخرة ليسا بالظلمة والضياء بل لهما علامة أخرى بتجلى من التجليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to the precise, remarkable reckoning in the sun's and moon's ordered movements.
rows.anchor: ذلك التسيير البديع بالحساب المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty's determination is His subduing the sun and moon and directing them in their particular courses.
rows.anchor: الذي قهرهما وسيرهما على الوجه المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the benefits and interests of the sun and moon for creatures' worldly life and afterlife.
rows.anchor: بما فيهما من المنافع والمصالح المتعلقة بمعاش الخلق ومعادهم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Sa'di's Persian poem says clouds, wind, moon, sun, and firmament work so a person can receive bread without heedlessness; they obey God, so it is unfair for a person to disobey.
rows.anchor:
قال السعدي :
ابر وباد ومه وخورشيد وفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God arranged the stars in positions that vary north, south, east, and west.
rows.anchor: التي تختلف مواضعها من جهة الشمال والجنوب والصبا والدبور

words: لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ بِهَا فِى ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars guide people on land and sea in the darkness of night; the darkness is associated with those settings because that is when guidance by stars is needed.
rows.anchor: في ظلمات الليل في البر والبحر وإضافتها إليهما للملابسة

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi explains that travelers identify routes through deserts and seas at night by placing particular stars before, beside, or behind them.
rows.anchor: لتعرفوا بها الطرق من بلد إلى بلد في المفاوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars also adorn the sky and stone devils, among other benefits.
rows.anchor: وهي أنها زينة السماء ورمي الشياطين وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained, detail by detail, the signs demonstrating His power; those who know benefit from them.
rows.anchor: أي بينا الآيات الدالة على قدرتنا فصلا فصلا

words: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people descend from Adam, and Eve was created from one of Adam's ribs; even Jesus began from Mary, who was created from her parents, so common origin should make people more affectionate toward one another.
rows.anchor: من نفس آدم وحدها فإنه خلقنا جميعا منه وخلق أمنا حواء من ضلع من أضلاع آدم

words: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍ
rows.speaker: أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: The people of allusion say that just as Adam was created first and human descendants came from him, Muhammad's spirit was created before other spirits and they came from it; Adam is father of humans and Muhammad father of spirits.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى كما خلق آدم ابتداء وجعل أولاده منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr and mustawda' are both place-denoting verbal nouns, nominative as subjects with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما مصدر ميمي مرفوع على الابتداء والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted sense is that a person has a place of settlement in the loins or above the earth, and a place of deposit in the womb or beneath the earth.
rows.anchor: أي فلكم استقرار في الأصلاب أو فوق الأرض واستيداع في الأرحام أو تحت الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father's backbone is the sperm's settled place, while the mother's womb is its deposit because it reaches her through another's action, like something entrusted to her.
rows.anchor: وجعل صلب الأب مستقر النطفة ورحم الأم مستودعا لها لأن النطفة حصلت في صلب الأب لا من قبل الغير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a son of Adam is a deposit among his family and will soon return to his owner.
rows.anchor: يا ابن آدم أنت وديعة في أهلك ويوشك أن تلحق بصاحبكم

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's poem says wealth and family are only deposits that must one day be returned; Bursevī adds that the heart too is a trust.
rows.anchor: وما المال والأهلون إلا وديعة ولا بد يوما أن ترد الودائع

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Sa'ib's Persian poem describes the heart's jewel as entrusted to one's care and urges the keeper not to neglect God's trust.
rows.anchor: ترا بكوهر دل كرده اند امانتدار نه دزد امانت حق را نكاه دار مخسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in 6:97 concern the cosmic creation, while those in 6:98 detail human creation; cosmic signs are more apparent and call for knowing, whereas subtle human signs call for discerning understanding.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر مع ذكر النجوم يعلمون ومع ذكر تخليق بني آدم يفقهون لأن ذلك إشارة إلى آيات الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiqh implies splitting and opening: a jurist probes rulings and truths and opens what is difficult, so the term suits subtle matters requiring close thought.
rows.anchor: وأصل تركيب الفقه يدل على الشق والفتح والفقيه العالم الذي يشق الأحكام ويفتش عن حقائقها

rows.speaker: الحدادي
rows.claim: Al-Haddadi defines fiqh linguistically as understanding speech and conventionally as deriving its meaning from principles; God is not called a jurist because He knows directly, not by inference.
rows.anchor: الفقه في اللغة هو الفهم لمعنى الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cosmic and human signs disclose God's wondrous work and call polytheists to tawhid, sincere believers to direct witnessing, and sinners to obedience and repentance of tongue and heart.
rows.anchor: ثم هذه الآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية تفصح عن صنع الله البديع وتدعو أهل الشرك إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Great blessings call for gratitude and recognition of their due; each person's path to realization follows the gift received, whether unification of divine acts, attributes, or essence.
rows.anchor: فإن الامتنان بذكر النعم الجليلة يستدعي شكرا لها ومعرفة لحقها ولكل قوم وفريق سلوك إلى طريق التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person must seek the Real; the ordered cosmic and human worlds are means to reach what is manifest through its manifestations, while heedlessness is the true veil.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد في طلب الحق فإن المقصود من ترتيب مقدمات العوالم آفاقية كانت أو أنفسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote tells how Shahin ibn Shuja al-Kirmani, a king who had gone hunting, met a youth riding a lion among wild beasts; the youth rebuked his heedlessness and worldliness, saying God gave the world to help people serve Him.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن الشيخ أبا الفوارس شاهين بن شجاع الكرماني رحمه الله خرج للصيد وهو ملك كرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the anecdote, an old woman brought the youth water, and Shahin found it exceptionally sweet; the youth said the world had been assigned to serve him, supplying what he needed, and quoted God telling the world to serve whoever serves Him and enslave whoever serves it; Shahin repented.
rows.anchor: هذه الدنيا وكلها الله إلى خدمتي فما احتجت إلى شيء إلا أحضرته إلي حين يخطر ببالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian poem continued from the prior segment asks God to keep the speaker serving at His door and never cut him off from His presence.
rows.anchor: خدمت لما إن صرت من خدمك ودار عندي السرور من نعمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent from heaven is specifically rain.
rows.anchor: {الذى أنزل من السمآء مآء} خاصا هو المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from speaking of God in the third person to 'We brought forth' uses the plural of majesty, not a plural of number.
rows.anchor: فالنون للعظمة لا الجمع فإن الملك العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain produces plants such as wheat, barley, pomegranate, and apple; 'every thing' is restricted to what grows, not stones or other non-growing things.
rows.anchor: ينبت كنبات الحنطة والشعير والرمان والتفاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabt and nabat mean growth from the earth, whether a woody tree with a trunk or a plant without one.
rows.anchor: والنبت والنبات ما يخرج من الأرض من الناميات سواء كان له ساق كالشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks whether making rain a cause means God needs instruments; Bursevī answers that rain leads to growth but does not generate it, and God can grow plants without rain.
rows.anchor: لأن المطر سبب يؤدي إلى النبات وليس بمولود له والله تعالى قادر على إنبات النبات بدون المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An agent needs a means only when the action is impossible without it; a ladder is not necessary for climbing a roof if the climber can ascend without one.
rows.anchor: إنما يكون الفاعل بالسبب مستعينا بذلك السبب إذا لم يمكنه فعل ذلك الشيء إلا بذلك السبب
